[PREFERENCE] User is interested in digital product design.  
[EVENT] User asked about who a digital product designer is.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A digital product designer is responsible for designing and creating digital products such as websites, mobile apps, software, and other digital interfaces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The main goal of a digital product designer is to create an intuitive and user-friendly digital product that meets the needs of the target audience while also meeting business goals and objectives.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Digital product designers typically work in a cross-functional team that includes product managers, developers, and other stakeholders.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Digital product designers are involved in the entire product development process, from researching user needs to designing user interfaces, to testing and refining the product.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The role requires a strong understanding of user experience (UX) design, user interface (UI) design, visual design, and human-computer interaction.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Digital product designers should also have a good understanding of the latest design trends, technologies, and tools used in the industry.  
[EVENT] User requested a comprehensive beginners curriculum for learning digital product design.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] A comprehensive beginners curriculum for learning digital product design was provided, divided into different modules.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Module 1: Introduction to Digital Product Design includes topics such as understanding the basics, history, types of digital products, importance in business, and the design process.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Module 2: User Research includes understanding user research, conducting interviews and surveys, analyzing data, creating personas, and mapping user journeys.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Module 3: User Experience Design (UX) includes principles of UX design, user-centered design, wireframes, prototypes, information architecture, navigation design, and usability testing.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Module 4: User Interface Design (UI) includes principles of UI design, visual hierarchy, color theory, typography, UI design elements, accessibility, and high-fidelity prototypes.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Module 5: Interaction Design includes principles of interaction design, creating interactive prototypes, animation, micro-interactions, and designing for different devices.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Module 6: Design Tools and Software includes understanding design software, best practices, design systems, and collaboration tools.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Module 7: Designing for Business includes understanding business goals, balancing needs, effective messaging, and measuring design performance.
